decisions.reason: Selecting the integrated board's mounting orientation for a clean layout does not remove or change the candidate's specific battery-connector access, placement, orientation, or mounting-hole constraints.
The legacy interboard-alignment requirement was already eliminated under the single-board architecture; choosing the integrated board's orientation does not further change that retained removal fact.
The source selects mounting orientation and enclosure-fit strategy without changing the established single-board architecture or board count.
Fitting the case to the integrated board does not necessarily change the legacy main board's recorded dimensions or prototype dimension flexibility.
Board-orientation flexibility does not alter the requirement to place the ESP32 antenna at the PCB edge.
The mounting-orientation and enclosure-fit decision has no entailed effect on the legacy main board's four-layer stack.
Choosing the orientation that yields the cleanest connector layout does not change the cost goal, component-selection policy, integrated architecture, or elimination of interboard connectors.
The source does not change the required external sensor connectors, their fanout role, or the policy of retaining individual sensor cables.
The board-orientation choice does not change USB data lines, connector sourceability, or the USB-C programming-port role.
The source decision does not alter I2C speed, pull-up values or location, series-resistor policy, or signal-conditioning topology.
Allowing the enclosure to follow the selected board orientation does not change the external backlight's electrical design, supply options, placement behind the display, or required status.
The mechanical orientation and enclosure-fit decision has no entailed effect on the battery's electrical protection requirements or configured protection components.
